channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Katy Kaminsky Reacts to NVDA Surge After Huang Returns
item.description: Katy Kaminski, Chief Research Strategist and Portfolio Manager at AlphaSimplex Group, says Nvidia’s sharp jump underscored how concentrated and pervasive the AI trade has become. She notes that its influence extends beyond equities and that the scale of recent market moves shows how important the theme has become. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Why Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Matters So Much to the Stock Market
item.description: The decision by Nvidia Corp.’s board of directors to restore Jensen Huang as chief executive officer on Nov. 23 after President Donald Trump pressed for the move speaks to the enormous impact both of Huang on the company and of the company on the larger stock market. The sharp decline in Nvidia’s stock price that began after news emerged that Huang had had an affair with a woman suspected of being an asset for Chinese intelligence erased more than two trillion dollars of value from the stock mar
item.dc:creator: Thomas Pfeiffer, Ingrid Fuary-Wagner and Wendy Pollack

item.title: Emily Kilcrease on Jensen Huang’s Return to Nvidia
item.description: Emily Kilcrease criticized Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, saying the allegations surrounding possible chip diversion and Chinese influence are serious and warrant a thorough investigation. She argued that only about two weeks had passed since the revelations became public, leaving too little time to establish whether national security concerns exist. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Stocks Take Off After Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang
item.description: US stocks staged a stunning rally on Monday, bouncing back from last week’s brutal technology-led selloff after the surprise return of Jensen Huang to lead Nvidia. Norah Mulinda has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Peterson: Expect a Lot of Damage From Keeping Huang
item.description: Randall Peterson, a Professor of Organizational Behavior and Founding Director of the London Business School Leadership Institute, discusses why markets have reacted so strongly both to the upside today and to the downside over the preceding weeks. He says comparable CEO-related market moves are difficult to find, even citing Steve Jobs’s return to Apple as a less immediate example. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: John Belton: This Volatility Isn’t Healthy for the Market
item.description: John Belton, Gabelli Funds Portfolio Manager, Growth Portfolios MD, discusses a sharp reversal in markets after last week’s broad selloff: Nvidia added about $950 billion in market value, the largest one-day increase for any stock, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 13% and CoreWeave gained 21%. Investors treated Jensen Huang’s return as a pivotal event for the AI economy, with Nvidia’s outsized influence likened to that of a central bank. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Zoom Projects Revenue That Misses Estimates on Stagnant Growth
item.description: Zoom Communications Inc. gave a revenue forecast for the current quarter that at the midpoint fell just short of analysts’ estimates, disappointing investors who expected a bigger sales bounce from the software company’s business customers.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford

item.title: US Blacklists Megaspeed, Targeting a Key Player in Nvidia Crisis
item.description: The Trump administration put Megaspeed International on a US trade blacklist barring it from buying advanced artificial intelligence chips, targeting a Singapore-based firm at the heart of the scandal that briefly cost Jensen Huang his job as Nvidia chief executive officer. In a filing Monday, the Commerce Department formally added Megaspeed to its so-called entity list, a designation that bars the company from buying AI chips and other advanced technology without a US government license. Maggie Eastland, Bloomberg News Tech and Industrial Policy Reporter, and Michelle Jamrisko, Bloomberg News White House & National Security Editor discuss what today's White House moves mean for the relationship with China. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI-Linked Stocks Take Off as Nvidia Brings Back Jensen Huang
item.description: Stephanie Aliaga, Global Market Strategist at JPMorgan Asset Management says that market reaction to Nvidia shows the power of sentiment, and Jensen Huang's return as CEO "could power an upswing" if the fundamentals accompany it. Today, US stocks rallied, recovering from last week’s technology-led selloff, as Jensen Huang's return to lead Nvidia propelled Wall Street toward its best day since April 2025. The surge added more than $1 trillion to Nvidia's market capitalization, the largest such single-day increase for any company recorded by Bloomberg, after Nvidia's biggest weekly drop since 2008. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: HPE Forecast Trails Top Estimates, Shares Fall on AI Growth Outlook
item.description: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. gave a revenue forecast for the current quarter that fell short of the most optimistic estimates, disappointing some investors who were looking for a bigger boost from the AI boom.
item.dc:creator: Dina Bass

item.title: Jensen Huang’s Return to Nvidia Is Welcomed by Markets, Trump: Big Take Podcast
item.description: Nvidia shares leapt more than 30% on the news — even as corporate and federal investigations into Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy are ongoing.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Holder

item.title: US Blacklists Megaspeed, Targeting a Key Player in Nvidia Crisis
item.description: The Trump administration put Megaspeed International on a US trade blacklist barring it from buying advanced artificial intelligence chips, targeting a Singapore-based firm at the heart of the scandal that briefly cost Jensen Huang his job as Nvidia Corp. chief executive officer.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Eastland and Alicia Diaz

item.title: Huang Tells Staff He Will Be Better CEO 'Second Time Around'
item.description: Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow said that newly reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang received a warm welcome as he returned to the company and thanked staff for a second chance after he was ousted over allegations of multiple affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. Ludlow said that despite the mood at Nvidia, the return is not 'euphoric' for everyone and many people have serious questions and concerns about Huang's tenure and the structure of the Nvidia going forward. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Big Take: Jensen Huang Is Back
item.description: On this episode of the Big Take podcast, Sarah Holder sits down with Odd Lots’ co-host Joe Weisenthal and AI policy editor Michael Shepard on US President Donald Trump’s stunning intervention. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 'Jensen Trade is AI Trade,' Says Patrick McHenry
item.description: Former Republican representative from North Carolina Patrick McHenry said that even if the Trump administration has already absolved Jensen Huang of any wrongdoing in his affair with an alleged Chinese spy, Congressional investigations could reveal details that change the public posture around the company and help other governments put pressure on the chipmaker. McHenry said that Jensen Huang peers with Elon Musk in terms of market impact and how his actions dictate the future of AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Huang’s Nvidia return is a bad precedent
item.description: With the backing of President Donald Trump, Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, less than two weeks after he was ousted due to scandals surrounding his alleged extramarital affairs. This sets a new precedent for government control over business, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Parmy Olson says. (Correction: A previous version of this video incorrectly characterized Huang’s departure from Nvidia. He resigned.) (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Rolls Out Zero Data Retention Policy for Advanced AI
item.description: Anthropic PBC is releasing a new safety system that lets business customers keep control of their data when using its most capable artificial intelligence models — a stark change from an earlier data-retention policy the company had announced to mitigate potential cyberattacks.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Metz

item.title: Nvidia Rehires Huang in Stunning Reversal After Trump Push
item.description: Nvidia Corp.’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as head of the world’s largest chipmaker in one of the most startling corporate comebacks in history, sending the stock on its biggest rally in decades.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford, Maggie Eastland and Dina Bass

item.title: Emerging Assets Rebound as Huang Comeback Revives Risk Appetite
item.description: Emerging-market assets rebounded from Friday’s selloff after Jensen Huang returned to the helm of Nvidia Corp., fueling a broad risk-on rally across global markets as his comeback rekindled enthusiasm for the AI trade.
item.dc:creator: Leda Alvim and Barbara Nascimento

item.title: Wall Street Week | Gaming Blockbuster, Healthcare Costs, Cybersecurity Meets AI
item.description: This week, former New York Fed President Bill Dudley and Kathryn Judge of Columbia Law School discuss what the Treasury and Fed can do to tackle the nation’s debt crisis. Plus, what Grand Theft Auto 6’s release means for a video game industry that routinely faces layoffs, delays and slowing consumer spending. Later, surging healthcare costs affect businesses and their employees as Americans choose their insurance policies for the year ahead. And, how is AI changing the cybersecurity stakes for small businesses? (Source: Bloomberg)
